question.question: When an applied implicit joint configuration owes automatic exit and its internal leave proposal is rejected during leadership transfer, does transfer abort restore an implementation-owned continuation without an unrelated client proposal?
question.importance: A stranded joint configuration would retain the outgoing quorum requirement and can obstruct subsequent membership changes; no safety violation or global unavailability has been demonstrated.
contexts: Implicit joint configuration on a leader
Transfer active when committed configuration application completes
Transfer timeout with continued viable joint quorum
event_paths: ApplyConfChange -> application completion -> appliedTo -> Step(MsgProp) -> transfer rejection

question.trigger_rationale: Exploration reached the actual committed-change/application/transfer overlap through public APIs. Transfer cleared at tick 10, while joint AutoLeave remained at tick 40 with queues and Ready work drained. A later ordinary command restored exit. Source callers of appliedTo are entry application and snapshot completion; abort itself does not retry. A fixed full-state recurrence check can distinguish an autonomous delayed continuation from the observed trigger dependency.

obligation.description: After an implicit joint configuration has been committed and applied, Raft must retain or restore an internally driven continuation to leave the joint configuration when an overlapping leadership transfer aborts, provided leadership and a viable joint quorum remain stable and required storage, application, ticks and network work continue. Completing that automatic transition must not depend on an unrelated new client proposal.

scope.description: Implementation-owned automatic joint-exit continuation under an aborted transfer with stable leadership and viable joint quorum.
assumptions: Only network TimeoutNow loss is needed in the prefix; ordinary Raft messages continue to be delivered
Caller performs ordered persistence, committed configuration application and completion acknowledgments
The suffix contains regular ticks and drains all resulting work without unrelated new proposals
No crash, Byzantine input, invalid membership operation or skipped caller completion
excluded: No fixed numeric deadline or claim that finite waiting alone proves non-progress
No consensus-safety, client response-time or whole-cluster unavailability claim
No claim that later application work or a new election cannot recover

pending: A fresh fixed direct check and correspondence review are required; exploration is construction knowledge.

grounding.derivation: ConfChangeTransitionJointImplicit specifies automatic exit by a zero configuration proposal; ConfState.AutoLeave and tracker.Config explicitly assign this transition to Raft when possible, contrasting explicit mode where the application must propose it. The application already proposed and applied the entering configuration. appliedTo implements the internal continuation and explicitly anticipates rejection during transfer and a later retry. This establishes implementation ownership beyond the word automatic alone. Under retained leadership and a viable joint quorum after transfer abort, absence of an unrelated client command must not permanently eliminate that continuation. Generic caller retry duties for external proposals do not require inventing new client work to drive an already applied automatic transition. No numeric deadline is claimed; only a closed repeating execution without an internally driven transition would witness the requirement gap.
grounding.applicability: Committed implicit joint change applied in order; transfer overlaps its application acknowledgment and later aborts; eligible leader retained, viable incoming/outgoing quorums, reliable ongoing ordinary message delivery and ticks, storage/application work completed; no crash or new client commands.
unresolved: Fixed recurrence observations and semantic correspondence have not yet been executed/reviewed.
alternatives: A later committed application callback legitimately retries and may recover; a new leader may generate such progress with its empty entry. These do not promise an event in the stable-leader, application-free suffix.
